Feluda.description: A sharp-eyed private investigator and the protagonist of the story who leads the investigation into Radharaman Samaddar's death.

Monimohan Samaddar.description: Radharaman Samaddar's nephew who seeks Feluda's professional help regarding his uncle's mysterious death.

Radharaman Samaddar.description: A reclusive and tight-fisted former lawyer and musician who recently died under mysterious circumstances, leaving behind a complex legacy.

Muralidhar.description: Radharaman Samaddar's only son, now deceased.

Dharanidhar.description: Radharaman's grandson and Muralidhar's son who left his studies to join the theatre; he is suspected to be the actor known as Sanjay Lahiri.

Anukul.description: Radharaman Samaddar's old servant who provided information about his daily habits.

Bamungachhi.description: A suburb of Calcutta where Radharaman Samaddar built his house and lived as a recluse.

Calcutta.description: A major city in India, now known as Kolkata.

Lake Place.description: A locality in Calcutta where Monimohan Samaddar lives.

Bombay.description: A major Indian city, now known as Mumbai.

Bhawanipore.description: A neighborhood in Calcutta where Monimohan runs his printing press.

Eureka Press.description: The printing press owned and operated by Monimohan Samaddar.

Charminar.description: A popular brand of Indian cigarettes.

Austin.description: A British car brand; Radharaman owned a second-hand Austin.

jatra.description: A traditional Bengali folk theatre form.

Babu.description: A respectful term used in India to address men, often appended to a name.

almirah.description: A freestanding cupboard or wardrobe, commonly used in Indian households.

will.description: A legal document stating a person's wishes regarding the disposal of their property after death.

Abani Sen.description: Radharaman Samaddar's neighbor and father of Sadhan; he is a florist with a shop in New Market who informed Monimohan about the heart attack.

Sadhan.description: Abani Sen's ten-year-old son, who was close to Radharaman Samaddar and spends time around the house.

Surajit Dasgupta.description: A collector of musical instruments who wanted to purchase some from Radharaman Samaddar.

Jessore Road.description: A major road in West Bengal, India, connecting Kolkata to Jessore in Bangladesh.

Barasat.description: A city near Kolkata, West Bengal, India, mentioned as a landmark on the way to Bamungachhi.

New Market.description: A historic and popular shopping area in central Kolkata, known for its variety of shops.

Minerva Hotel.description: A hotel located on Central Avenue in Calcutta, mentioned as the sender's address on a postcard.

Central Avenue.description: A prominent street in Kolkata, India.

Dehra Dun.description: A city in northern India, now called Dehradun, mentioned as the place where Surajit Dasgupta lives.

Iran.description: A country in the Middle East, referenced as the origin of the khamanche instrument.

England.description: A country in the United Kingdom, referenced as the origin of the melochord instrument.

Second World War.description: A global conflict from 1939 to 1945, referenced in relation to the German lock.

jalebis.description: A popular Indian sweet made by deep-frying batter in circular shapes and soaking them in sugar syrup.

mali.description: A gardener or person who tends to plants and gardens.

nursery.description: A place where plants are grown for sale, especially flowers and saplings.

chaddar.description: A traditional cloth or shawl, often used as a wrap or cover.

sitar.description: A plucked stringed instrument used in Indian classical music.

sarod.description: A fretless stringed instrument prominent in Indian classical music.

tanpura.description: A long-necked plucked string instrument that provides a drone in Indian classical music.

tabla.description: A pair of hand-played drums used in Indian classical and popular music.

Dadu.description: A Bengali term for grandfather or an elderly male figure.

melochord.description: A rare keyboard instrument, referenced as being made in England.

Mr Mondol.description: Owner of Mondol & Co., a music shop in Lal Bazaar, who provides information about musical instruments.

Topshe.description: The narrator and Feluda's cousin, who assists him in his investigations.

Poltu.description: Topshe's friend, from whom a harmonium is borrowed.

Bihar.description: An Indian state where Muralidhar worked before his death.

Spiegler.description: A German company that produced musical instruments, referenced in a catalogue.

Manchalok.description: A theatre journal Feluda contacts for information about Sanjay Lahiri.

Modern Opera.description: A theatre group where Sanjay Lahiri performed lead roles.

Jalpaiguri.description: A town in West Bengal, India, where the theatre group is currently located.

National Museum.description: A museum visited by Feluda and Topshe to research musical instruments.

Mahabharata.description: An ancient Indian epic, referenced in the museum's musical instrument section.

Free School Street.description: A street in Calcutta known for its shops, including music stores.

Lal Bazaar.description: A locality in Calcutta, home to Mondol & Co. music shop.

Mondol & Co..description: A music shop in Lal Bazaar, frequented by Mr Samaddar.

College Street.description: A street in Calcutta known for its bookstores, where Feluda buys books on music.

harmonium.description: A portable, hand-pumped keyboard instrument commonly used in Indian music.

sa re ga ma pa dha ni sa.description: Sa re ga ma pa dha ni sa, also known as sargam, are the seven basic notes of the Indian musical scale, equivalent to the Western do re mi.

lassi.description: A traditional Indian yogurt-based drink, served sweet or salty.

load shedding.description: A scheduled power outage, common in India, to reduce electricity consumption.

Dr Chintamoni Bose.description: Dr Chintamoni Bose is a heart specialist who accompanied Monimohan to Radharaman's house during his final moments and was present at the time of Radharaman’s death.

Srinath.description: The cook in Feluda's household, who brings tea during the investigation.

OC.description: Abbreviation for Officer-in-Charge, referring to the local police authority.

Inspector Dinesh Guin.description: Inspector Dinesh Guin is a police officer from the Barasat police station who appears during the investigation.

VIP Road.description: A major road in Kolkata, India, known for its heavy traffic.

Germany.description: Germany, referenced as German, is a country in Europe and the origin of the melochord and the lock.

airgun.description: A low-powered gun that uses compressed air to shoot pellets, often used by children for target practice.

Dettol.description: A popular antiseptic liquid widely used in India for cleaning wounds.
